question:
Which type of system did the leaders of independent India decide to adopt?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options:
A system that would promote the welfare of private enterprises

A system that would promote the welfare of few rather than all

A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few

A system that would promote the welfare of the government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few

Explanation:
The leaders of independent India decided to adopt a socialist and welfare-oriented system, aiming to promote the welfare of all citizens. This is reflected in the Preamble and Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Constitution. Article 38 directs the state to secure social, economic, and political justice, while Article 39 outlines goals like equal pay for equal work, equitable distribution of resources, and reducing economic inequality. This approach was influenced by Gandhian socialism and Nehruvian economic policies.

Extra Facts:
- The Preamble of the Indian Constitution includes the term 'social, economic, and political justice,' reflecting socialist goals.
- The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) added the word 'socialist' to the Preamble, declaring India a socialist republic.
- In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court held that the basic structure of the Constitution is based on socialist principles.

☛ What type of state is India? → Socialist, secular, democratic republic

options_hi:

solution_hi:

Explanation:
स्वतंत्र भारत के नेताओं ने एक समाजवादी और कल्याणकारी राज्य की स्थापना का निर्णय लिया था, जिसका उद्देश्य सभी नागरिकों के कल्याण को बढ़ावा देना था। यह संविधान के प्रस्तावना और भाग IV (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व) में स्पष्ट रूप से परिलक्षित होता है। अनुच्छेद 38 राज्य को सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश देता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 39 समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन, संसाधनों का समान वितरण और आर्थिक असमानता को कम करने जैसे लक्ष्य निर्धारित करता है। यह दृष्टिकोण गांधीवादी समाजवाद और नेहरूवादी आर्थिक नीतियों से प्रभावित था।

Extra Facts:
- भारतीय संविधान का प्रस्तावना में 'सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय' शब्द समाजवादी लक्ष्यों को दर्शाता है।
- 42वें संविधान संशोधन (1976) ने प्रस्तावना में 'समाजवादी' शब्द जोड़ा, जिससे भारत को एक समाजवादी गणराज्य घोषित किया गया।
- मिनर्वा मिल्स केस (1980) में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि संविधान का मूल ढांचा समाजवादी सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है।

question:
When did India declare itself a Sovereign, Democratic and Republic state with the adoption of the Constitution?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: 14 November 1952
2 October 1949
15 August 1947
26 January 1950
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26 January 1950

Explanation:
India adopted its Constitution on 26 January 1950 and declared itself a Sovereign, Democratic, and Republic state on the same day. This date was chosen because, on 26 January 1930, the Indian National Congress had proclaimed 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence). Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States,' reflecting its sovereignty, democracy, and republican system.

Extra Facts:
- The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into effect on 26 January 1950.
- 15 August 1947- The Indian Constitution is the world's longest written constitution.

question:
According to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, India is a __________ country.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Religious
Liberal
Aristocratic
Republic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Republic

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India as a "Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic". The term Republic signifies that the head of the state (President) is elected indirectly by the people, not hereditary. This is also reflected in Articles 52 to 78 of the Constitution. The Preamble is the foundation of the Constitution and was recognized as part of the "Basic Structure" in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

Extra Facts:
- The Preamble was amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976), which added the words "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity".
- India’s President is elected under Article 54 by an electoral college, reflecting the Republic concept.
- The phrase "We, the People of India" in the Preamble signifies that the power of the Constitution derives from the people.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है गणराज्य (Republic)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में भारत को एक "संप्रभु, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य" घोषित किया गया है। गणराज्य (Republic) का अर्थ है कि देश का प्रमुख (राष्ट्रपति) जनता द्वारा अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से चुना जाता है, न कि वंशानुगत। यह संविधान के अनुच्छेद 52 से अनुच्छेद 78 तक के प्रावधानों में भी स्पष्ट है। प्रस्तावना संविधान का आधार है और इसे केसवानंद भारती मामले (1973) में संविधान का "आधारभूत ढांचा" माना गया।

Extra Facts:
- प्रस्तावना को 42वें संविधान संशोधन (1976) द्वारा संशोधित किया गया, जिसमें "समाजवादी", "धर्मनिरपेक्ष" और "एकता व अखंडता" शब्द जोड़े गए।
- भारत का राष्ट्रपति अनुच्छेद 54 के तहत एक निर्वाचक मंडल द्वारा चुना जाता है, जो गणराज्य की अवधारणा को दर्शाता है।
- प्रस्तावना में "हम भारत के लोग" शब्द संविधान की शक्ति का स्रोत जनता को बताते हैं।

question:
Which of the following word sequences is correct as per the Preamble to the Constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic
Secular, democratic, secular, socialist, sovereign
Sovereign, secular, socialist, democratic, republic
Socialist, secular, democratic, republic, sovereign
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic

Explanation:
The correct sequence of words in the Preamble to the Indian Constitution is: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic. This sequence was finalized after the addition of the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976). The Preamble declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic. This order reflects the basic structure of the Constitution, upheld by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) as part of the 'Basic Structure Doctrine'.

Extra Facts:
The Preamble is called the 'Soul of the Constitution'. The words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment. The Preamble outlines the objectives of the Constitution and is interpretable by courts. In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution, but this was overturned in the Kesavananda Bharati case.

question:
Which of the following is NOT mentioned in ‘Liberty’ as per the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Faith and worship
Thought
Trust and hope
Expression
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Trust and hope

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution mentions 'Liberty' as encompassing thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship, which are linked to Fundamental Rights like Article 19 (freedom of speech) and Articles 25-28 (religious freedom). However, 'Trust and hope' is not explicitly mentioned in the Preamble. This option is ambiguous and lacks constitutional backing compared to the other three.

Extra Facts:
- The Preamble is termed the 'Soul of the Constitution'. It was deemed non-justiciable in the Berubari Case (1960) but declared an integral part of the Constitution in the Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973).
- Along with Liberty, the Preamble highlights Equality, Fraternity, and Justice, making India a Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
- The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

question:
The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a ___________system of government.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: unitary
parliamentary
monarchical
presidential
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is parliamentary

Explanation:
The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a parliamentary system of government. This system is inspired by the British Westminster model, where the executive (Council of Ministers) is accountable to the legislature (Parliament). Article 74 of the Constitution provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. As per Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This system ensures democratic values and accountability.

Extra Facts:
- India's parliamentary system is based on the Westminster model.
- The President is the constitutional head, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head.
- The Council of Ministers must resign if it loses majority in the Lok Sabha (Article 75(2)).
- The parliamentary system features a bicameral legislature (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).

राजतंत्रीय

Explanation:

- संसदीय प्रणाली में द्विसदनीय विधायिका (लोकसभा और राज्यसभा) होती है।

Explanation:
The term 'Republic' in the Indian Constitution signifies that the head of the state (President) is elected, not hereditary. This is reflected in the Preamble, which declares India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic. Articles 54 and 55 outline the election process of the President, where an electoral college elects the President. This system establishes India as a republic, where the highest office is not inherited but chosen indirectly by the people.

Extra Facts:

- The President's term is 5 years, with eligibility for re-election (Article 56).
- India's first President, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, was an elected head, not hereditary.
- The United Kingdom is not a republic, as it has a hereditary monarch.

Explanation:
In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble of the Constitution can be amended, but its 'Basic Structure' cannot be altered. This landmark judgment was delivered by a 13-judge Constitution Bench, which interpreted Article 368 and imposed limitations on Parliament's amending power. The case also clarified that the Preamble is part of the Constitution, as affirmed by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976).

Extra Facts:

question:
An introductory statement in a constitution that states the reasons and guiding values of the constitution is called:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Article
Fundamental Rights
Preamble
Clause
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Preamble

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Constitution is an introductory statement that outlines the objectives, guiding principles, and ideals of the constitution. It is often called the 'soul' of the Constitution and explains the reasons behind its enactment. The Preamble of the Indian Constitution includes terms like 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic', reflecting its core values. It was amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976), which added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is part of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

Extra Facts:
☛ The Preamble is called the 'key to the Constitution' as it summarizes its essence.
☛ The phrase 'We, the People of India' signifies that the power of the Constitution flows from the people.
☛ It aids the judiciary in interpreting constitutional provisions.
☛ The Preamble can be amended under Article 368, but its 'Basic Structure' cannot be altered.

question:
On 26 January 1950 India became:

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: a socialist and secular state
a sovereign, democratic, republic state
an independent state
a unitary state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a sovereign, democratic, republic state

Explanation:
On 26 January 1950, India became a 'sovereign, democratic, republic state', as clearly mentioned in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. With the enforcement of the Constitution, India established its sovereignty (independent decision-making authority), democratic governance (government elected by the people), and republic (an elected head of state in the form of the President). The terms 'socialist' and 'secular' were added to the Preamble later through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) and were not part of the original text in 1950.

Extra Facts:
- The Preamble of the Indian Constitution is often called its 'soul'.
- 26 January was chosen because it marked the Purna Swaraj Day observed in 1930 during the freedom struggle.
- The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950.
- Republic Day commemorates the enforcement of the Indian Constitution.

question:

a federal state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a secular state

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Secular' state. This term was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976). Secularism means that India recognizes all religions equally and has no official state religion. Articles 25-28 of the Constitution guarantee the right to religious freedom.

Extra Facts:

- The terms 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added by the 42nd Amendment.

question:

The slogan of the French Revolution was "Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité", which influenced democratic values worldwide. The Preamble is considered the 'soul' of the Indian Constitution, embodying justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.

- The French Revolution influenced not only the Indian Constitution but also many other constitutions globally.

question:

The term 'Federalism' is not explicitly mentioned in the original text of the Indian Constitution, although India has a federal structure. भारत को एक 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' राज्य के रूप में संविधान की प्रस्तावना में वर्णित किया गया है। यह शब्द 42वें संविधान संशोधन (1976) के द्वारा प्रस्तावना में जोड़ा गया था। धर्मनिरपेक्षता का अर्थ है कि भारत सभी धर्मों के प्रति तटस्थ रहता है और किसी भी धर्म को राजधर्म का दर्जा नहीं देता। यह संविधान के मूल ढांचे का हिस्सा है, जैसा कि केसवानंद भारती मामले (1973) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा स्पष्ट किया गया था।

Extra Facts:
- प्रस्तावना को संविधान का 'परिचय पत्र' कहा जाता है, जिसमें संविधान के मूल उद्देश्यों का उल्लेख है।
- धर्मनिरपेक्षता के सिद्धांत को अनुच्छेद 25-28 (मौलिक अधिकार) में भी समर्थन मिलता है, जो धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता की गारंटी देते हैं।
- राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों (DPSP) में अनुच्छेद 44 समान नागरिक संहिता से संबंधित है, न कि धर्मनिरपेक्षता से।

question:
Which of the following is NOT a political philosophy of the Indian Constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Sensitive for the historically disadvantaged groups
Open to community values
Sensitive to the needs of religious and linguistic minorities
Non-committal to building a common national identity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is d (Non-committal to building a common national identity)

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution's political philosophy is inclusive, egalitarian, and pluralistic. It is sensitive to historically disadvantaged groups (Articles 15, 16, 17), community values (Articles 25-28), and religious/linguistic minorities (Articles 29-30). However, the Constitution is committed to building a common national identity, as reflected in the Preamble ("India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic") and Article 1 ("India as a Union of States"). Thus, option d is incorrect as it contradicts the Constitution's core philosophy.

Extra Facts:
- The Preamble defines India's core values: justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
- Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) expects citizens to promote national unity.
- In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court introduced the "Basic Structure" doctrine, which includes secularism and democracy.

निम्नलिखित में से क्या भारतीय संविधान का राजनीतिक दर्शन नहीं है?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options_hi: ऐतिहासिक रूप से वंचित समूहों के प्रति संवेदनशील
सामुदायिक मूल्यों के प्रति उदारवादी
धार्मिक और भाषाई अल्पसंख्यकों की अवश्यकताओं के प्रति संवेदनशील
एक सर्वनिष्ठ राष्ट्रीय पहचान बनाने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध नहीं है
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है d (एक सर्वनिष्ठ राष्ट्रीय पहचान बनाने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध नहीं है)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का राजनीतिक दर्शन समावेशी, समतामूलक और बहुलवादी है। यह ऐतिहासिक रूप से वंचित समूहों (अनुच्छेद 15, 16, 17), सामुदायिक मूल्यों (अनुच्छेद 25-28), और धार्मिक/भाषाई अल्पसंख्यकों (अनुच्छेद 29-30) के प्रति संवेदनशील है। हालाँकि, संविधान एक सर्वनिष्ठ राष्ट्रीय पहचान बनाने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध है, जैसा कि प्रस्तावना में "भारत एक सम्पूर्ण प्रभुत्वसम्पन्न समाजवादी पंथनिरपेक्ष लोकतंत्रात्मक गणराज्य" और अनुच्छेद 1 ("भारत राज्यों का संघ है") में दर्शाया गया है। इसलिए, विकल्प d गलत है क्योंकि यह संविधान के मूल दर्शन के विपरीत है।

Extra Facts:
- संविधान की प्रस्तावना भारत के मूल्यों – न्याय, स्वतंत्रता, समानता और बंधुत्व को परिभाषित करती है।
- अनुच्छेद 51A (मौलिक कर्तव्य) नागरिकों से राष्ट्रीय एकता को बढ़ावा देने की अपेक्षा करता है।
- केसवानंद भारती मामला (1973) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने संविधान के "मूल ढाँचे" की अवधारणा दी, जिसमें धर्मनिरपेक्षता और लोकतंत्र शामिल हैं।

question:
Secularism is a feature of the Indian Constitution, which means:

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: The State does not promote any religion.
The State promotes the religion of the minority community.
The State promotes the religion of the majority community.
The State can promote any religion.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The State does not promote any religion.

Explanation:
In the Indian Constitution, secularism means that the state does not endorse any particular religion and remains neutral towards all religions. This principle was added to the Preamble through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976). Articles 25 to 28 guarantee the right to religious freedom, allowing all citizens to practice their faith freely. The Supreme Court, in the S.R. Bommai case (1994), clarified that secularism is a basic feature of the Indian Constitution.

Extra Facts:
Indian secularism differs from the Western model. Here, the state treats all religions equally but can also intervene in religious matters, such as enforcing social reforms under Article 25(2). In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court declared secularism part of the Constitution's 'Basic Structure', which even Parliament cannot alter.

राज्य किसी भी धर्म को बढ़ावा दे सकता है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है राज्य किसी भी धर्म को बढ़ावा नहीं देता है।

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में धर्मनिरपेक्षता का अर्थ है कि राज्य किसी भी धर्म को विशेष दर्जा नहीं देता है और सभी धर्मों के प्रति तटस्थ रहता है। यह संविधान के प्रस्तावना में 1976 के 42वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। अनुच्छेद 25 से 28 तक धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता के अधिकारों की गारंटी दी गई है, जिसमें सभी नागरिकों को अपने धर्म का पालन करने की स्वतंत्रता दी गई है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने एस.आर. बोम्मई केस (1994) में स्पष्ट किया कि धर्मनिरपेक्षता भारतीय संविधान की मूल विशेषता है।

Extra Facts:
